definition: Edict means an order or decree issued by an authority.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word edict. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know edict should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By royal edict, no lantern could burn in the harbor town past the curfew bell.
A suggestion is the mildest word here — it can be declined with a smile, while an edict cannot be declined at all.
A directive stops short of an edict: it instructs and expects compliance, but an edict carries the full take-it-or-else weight of the authority who issued it.

A decree is the edict's near-twin, an order issued whole from a throne or a bench — the word stays in royal and judicial robes. Edict travels further down: any authority's take-it-or-else order, and in offices it adds an eye-roll at a boss playing emperor.

A proclamation is a public announcement, made to be heard widely, and it need not bind anyone — holidays and honors get proclaimed. An edict commands: it arrives from above, finished, and must be obeyed. A proclamation informs the crowd; an edict tells the crowd what it will do.
